Pronunciation note for this grammar point:
Nominalised forms shift the stress: implement /ˈɪm.plɪ.ment/ but implementation /ˌɪm.plɪ.menˈteɪ.ʃən/, with the main stress on the syllable before -tion.

elements.content: Grammar focus: Nominalisation & Register.

Nominalise when the action, not the actor, is the topic: the implementation of the policy took two years. Keep the agent in a possessive when responsibility matters: their refusal delayed the audit. Limit yourself to one nominalisation per clause, and keep a verb in the sentence so it still moves.

verb → noun — names the action: implement → implementation
adjective → noun — names the quality: refuse → refusal
of-phrase — carries the original object: the implementation of the policy
possessive — keeps the agent visible: their refusal to publish
there + noun — presents a change: there was a sharp rise in complaints
nominal + verb — one main verb per clause: the introduction of the levy provoked the strike
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Which is the nominalised version?
options: Their refusal to publish delayed the audit.

elements.content: 2. Complete: 'There was a sharp ___ in complaints.'
3. What does the agent become in 'their refusal'?
Read and listen: three examples in context.

When we automate the line, costs fall. — The automation of the line reduces costs. (Clause becomes subject.)
They refused to publish the data. — Their refusal to publish the data delayed the audit. (Agent moves into a possessive.)
Complaints rose sharply. — There was a sharp rise in complaints. (Manner becomes an adjective.)
What do you observe?

Nominalisation turns a verb or adjective into the head of a noun phrase: implement → the implementation of, refuse → their refusal to, rise → a sharp rise in. The original subject either becomes a possessive (their refusal) or disappears (the implementation of the policy), and the original verb's object becomes an of-phrase.
1. What happens to the agent in 'the implementation of the policy'?
options: It becomes the subject of the sentence.

elements.content: 2. Which is more formal?
options: The automation of the line reduces costs.

elements.content: State the rule in one sentence, without looking at the table.
Freer production: Can transform spoken technical explanations into formal executive reports using nominalization

Success criteria:
- I can turn a clause into a noun phrase.
- I can keep the agent in a possessive when it matters.
- I can stop compressing before the sentence stops moving.
Role play: put your position in ninety seconds; your partner notes every use of the target structure.
Frequent errors and correction:

❌ The implement of the policy took two years (verb used as a noun) → ✅ The implementation of the policy took two years
❌ The policy was implemented and it took two years and it was expensive (chain of clauses) → ✅ The implementation of the policy took two years and cost more than planned
Correct these sentences: say what is wrong, then give the right version.
Acceptable variants:

The withdrawal of the offer ended the negotiation.
Their withdrawal of the offer ended the negotiation.
There was a marked decline in applications after the change.
Adapt the same task to the group:

- Individual: five sentences with the structure, on the topic of the lesson.
- Pair: a ten-line dialogue where compound nouns carries the argument.
- Group: a six-minute debate, two sides, the structure required in every turn.
- Professional audience: transpose the structure into a memo.
- Academic audience: transpose it into a paragraph of analysis.

Second grammar point of the lesson: Compound Nouns. Decide the head noun first, then the modifier, then the spelling: two words by default, one word if the language has closed it, hyphens only when the compound modifies another noun
